About CALHN
At Central Adelaide (CALHN), we're shaping the future of health through excellence in clinical care, research, and innovation. As South Australia's largest health network, we deliver exceptional, safe and connected healthcare - for our patients, our community, and our people.

With more than 17,000 dedicated employees, every day at CALHN presents an opportunity to make a real impact-not because it's expected, but because our values guide us to be our best. Find out more about CALHN sites and services, our stories and the opportunities to be part of CALHN.

About the Role

Support vital health research by keeping grants on track from award to close. You will manage records, build trusted links with researchers and partners, and keep grant data accurate, timely and compliant across CALHN.

- Manage grant records pre and post award
- Maintain clear, accurate data and files
- Liaise with researchers and CALHN teams
- Support reporting and funding queries
- Engage with SA Health, funders and partners

About You

You bring calm, care and clarity to complex admin work, and enjoy supporting research teams to succeed.

- Strong admin skills, work well solo or with others
- Sharp eye for detail, meet deadlines under pressure
- Clear written and verbal communication with diverse groups
- Confident with Microsoft Office and data systems
- Knowledge of grants, research governance or finance admin processes

Why You'll Love It Here - CALHN benefits that matter

result.description:
Arais Care Pty Ltd is a dedicated NDIS service provider committed to delivering high-quality, person-centred support to people living with disability. We empower participants to achieve independence, dignity, social inclusion, and an improved quality of life through compassionate and professional care.
We are currently seeking a dedicated and compassionate Residential Care Officer to join our team in Dirranbandi, Queensland, a remote community. This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced care professional looking to build a rewarding career while making a meaningful difference in the lives of people living with disability.
Key Responsibilities
•	Ensure the safety, well-being, and dignity of residents with disability in a residential care setting.
•	Assess individual needs of NDIS participants to develop and implement personalised support, training, and life skills programs.
•	Support and empower residents to build independence, enhance daily living skills, and improve overall quality of life.
•	Facilitate and encourage resident participation in community activities to promote inclusion and social engagement.
•	Conduct client interviews to identify personal, emotional, and social challenges impacting their wellbeing.
•	Monitor and record resident progress, updating support plans as needed and maintaining accurate documentation.
•	Identify local resources and services related to health, housing, employment, and other areas relevant to NDIS participants.
•	Deliver structured skill-building and activity programs with limited supervision, both individually and as part of a team.
•	Liaise with families, support coordinators, community groups, service providers, and government agencies to ensure coordinated care.
•	Provide care and support in group homes and other supported accommodation settings, assisting with daily routines and personal tasks.
•	Assist with meal planning, preparation, and cooking according to resident needs and dietary requirements.
•	Help residents manage behavioural challenges by implementing Behaviour Support and Management Plans.
•	Refer participants to relevant allied health professionals, services, or community supports as appropriate.
•	Advocate for residents' rights and preferences in all aspects of care and community engagement.
•	Prepare reports, care documentation, and funding submissions in line with NDIS compliance and service requirements.
•	Respond to general enquiries, assist with special projects, and contribute to a safe, supportive, and person-centred environment.
•	Participate in team meetings, training, supervision, and continuous quality improvement initiatives.
•	Work effectively and independently in a remote community environment.
Essential Requirements
•	Completed at least a Diploma OR an overseas bachelor degree, preferably in Nursing or a related field; alternatively, at least three years of relevant experience may substitute for formal qualifications.
•	Minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience in disability support, residential care, aged care, or community services.
•	Willingness to work and live in Dirranbandi, Queensland (Remote).
•	Strong interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills.
•	Ability to work rotating shifts, including weekends, sleepovers, public holidays, and overnight shifts.
•	Current First Aid and CPR Certificate.
•	Current NDIS Worker Screening Clearance, or ability to obtain.
•	Police Clearance Certificate and ability to meet relevant character requirements.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team.
•	Understanding of person-centred practice and the rights, dignity, and choices of people with disability.
Desirable
•	Experience supporting participants with complex behaviours, psychosocial disability, or high-intensity support needs.
•	Knowledge and understanding of NDIS Practice Standards.
•	Experience with Positive Behaviour Support.
•	Medication competency.
•	Manual handling training.
•	Previous experience working in a rural or remote community.
•	Strong ability to adapt to the unique needs and challenges of remote service delivery.
What We Offer
•	Full-time permanent employment – minimum 38 hours per week.
•	Potential visa sponsorship for suitably qualified and eligible international candidates.
•	Supportive and inclusive workplace culture.
•	Ongoing professional development and training opportunities.
•	Career progression within a growing organisation.
•	Opportunity to work in a unique remote Queensland community.
•	Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of people living with disability.
How to Apply
To apply, please submit:
•	Your current resume (CV).
•	A cover letter outlining your suitability for the role.
•	Copies of relevant qualifications and licences/certificates.
Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.
Arais Care Pty Ltd is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and non-discriminatory recruitment practices. We encourage applications from suitably qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, disability, cultural background, or ethnicity.

Our client, Tjuwanpa Outstation Resource Centre (Aboriginal Corporation), plays a vital role in supporting the Western Arrarnta people across 37 outstations near Ntaria (Hermannsburg) in the Northern Territory. 

Since its establishment in 1984, Tjuwanpa has been responsible for administering government-funded programs relating to housing, water infrastructure, electricity, and employment services across the region. The organisation is recognised for its strong governance, effective financial management, and commitment to supporting Indigenous communities through sustainable and transparent operations.

Tjuwanpa is currently seeking a detail-oriented and reliable Accounts Clerk to support its finance and administrative functions. This role is critical in maintaining accurate financial records, assisting with day-to-day accounting processes, and ensuring compliance with organisational and regulatory requirements in a remote operational environment.

Key Responsibilities:
-	Process accounts payable and receivable transactions in a timely and accurate manner 
-	Prepare and reconcile invoices, purchase orders, and payment records 
-	Maintain financial records, ledgers, and supporting documentation 
-	Assist with bank reconciliations and monitor cash flow transactions 
-	Support payroll processing and maintain employee payment records 
-	Prepare basic financial reports and assist with monthly and annual reporting requirements 
-	Ensure compliance with internal financial procedures and relevant regulatory standards 
-	Liaise with suppliers, staff, and external stakeholders regarding financial matters 
-	Assist in budgeting processes and tracking of program expenditures 
-	Maintain accurate filing systems for financial documentation 
-	Support audits by preparing required documentation and reports 
-	Perform general administrative duties related to finance operations 

Qualifications and Experience:
-	AQF Certificate III in Accounting, Bookkeeping, or a related field

-	Previous experience in accounts payable/receivable or general accounting functions 
-	Experience working in a not-for-profit or community-based organisation (desirable) 

Skills and Attributes:
-	Strong numerical accuracy and attention to detail 
-	Good understanding of basic accounting principles and financial processes 
-	Proficiency in accounting software and Microsoft Office (especially Excel) 
-	Strong organisational and time management skills 
-	Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive financial information 
-	Effective communication skills and ability to liaise with diverse stakeholders 
-	Ability to work independently and as part of a team in a remote environment 

If you have the required skills and experience and are interested in contributing to a well-established organisation supporting Indigenous communities, we encourage you to apply.

Job Advertisement


Chef – Full Time
Business: Nepalaya Hospitality Group Pty Ltd (ABN 29 639 400 963) trading as Namaste Sydney
Location: 307 Pitt Street, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
Website: https://namasterestro.com.au/
Occupation: Chef (ANZSCO 351311)
Salary Range: AUD $75,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation
Employment Type: Full-time (minimum 38 hours per week)

Job Published: 27 July 2026
Applications Close: 28 August 2026

ABOUT THE BUSINESS
Nepalaya Hospitality Group Pty Ltd, trading as Namaste Sydney, operates a well-established full-service restaurant in the heart of Sydney CBD and forms part of a growing hospitality group with multiple hospitality venues. The restaurant has established a strong reputation for delivering quality à la carte dining, exceptional customer service, and a consistently high standard of hospitality.
Operating within a modern commercial kitchen, Namaste Sydney offers a diverse à la carte menu prepared using quality ingredients and established culinary techniques. The restaurant caters to a broad customer base in a fast-paced dining environment and is committed to maintaining excellence in food quality, presentation, operational efficiency, and compliance with Australian food safety standards.
Due to continued business growth and increasing customer demand, Nepalaya Hospitality Group Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced Chef to support kitchen operations, contribute to menu development, maintain consistent food quality, and assist in delivering an exceptional dining experience.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Chef will be responsible for planning, organising, and supervising food preparation and cooking activities within a busy commercial kitchen. Working collaboratively with management and kitchen staff, the successful candidate will ensure the consistent preparation and presentation of high-quality à la carte meals while maintaining operational efficiency, food safety compliance, and exceptional customer satisfaction.
The role requires a motivated hospitality professional with strong technical cooking skills, sound organisational capability, and the ability to coordinate kitchen activities during high-volume service periods. The successful candidate will also contribute to menu planning, food costing, stock management, quality assurance, and continuous improvement initiatives to support the efficient operation of the kitchen.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Core Culinary Operations
1.	Plan, organise and coordinate daily food preparation and cooking activities in accordance with operational requirements and anticipated service demands, ensuring kitchen readiness before each service period.
2.	Prepare, cook and present high-quality à la carte meals using a range of commercial cooking techniques while maintaining consistency in flavour, quality, presentation and portion control.
3.	Coordinate kitchen workflow during busy lunch and dinner services to ensure efficient meal production, timely service delivery, and effective communication between kitchen and front-of-house staff.
4.	Monitor food quality throughout all stages of preparation and service, ensuring ingredients are fresh and finished dishes consistently meet established quality standards.
5.	Maintain consistency in recipe execution, presentation standards and quality assurance across all menu offerings while ensuring customer expectations are consistently achieved.

Menu Planning and Development
1.	Assist in planning, reviewing and refining menus to maintain product quality, seasonal relevance and commercial competitiveness.
2.	Develop and recommend seasonal specials and new menu items based on customer preferences, market trends and ingredient availability.
3.	Support recipe standardisation, food costing and portion control to maximise operational efficiency while maintaining profitability.
4.	Evaluate customer feedback and menu performance to identify opportunities for continuous menu improvement and innovation.
5.	Participate in menu trials and product development initiatives to enhance the restaurant's culinary offerings.

Kitchen Operations and Inventory Management
1.	Manage inventory through effective ordering, receiving, storage and stock rotation procedures to maintain appropriate stock levels.
2.	Apply FIFO inventory management principles and monitor ingredient usage to minimise food wastage and maximise product quality.
3.	Conduct regular stocktakes and assist in monitoring food costs through effective inventory management practices.
4.	Liaise with suppliers regarding product quality, deliveries and stock availability to ensure uninterrupted kitchen operations.
5.	Maintain accurate purchasing, inventory and stock control records in accordance with business procedures.

Team Leadership and Kitchen Coordination
1.	Work collaboratively with kitchen and front-of-house teams to ensure efficient communication and coordinated service delivery.
2.	Support, mentor and provide day-to-day guidance to junior kitchen staff to maintain productivity, consistency and professional kitchen standards.
3.	Assist in allocating daily kitchen duties and coordinating workflow to maximise operational efficiency during service periods.
4.	Promote a positive, organised and team-oriented kitchen environment focused on quality, accountability and continuous improvement.
5.	Contribute to staff training by reinforcing food preparation techniques, food safety practices and operational procedures.

Food Safety, Hygiene and Compliance
1.	Maintain compliance with HACCP principles, NSW Food Authority requirements and all relevant food safety legislation.
2.	Ensure kitchen equipment, food preparation areas and storage facilities are maintained in a clean, organised and hygienic condition at all times.
3.	Monitor food storage temperatures, sanitation procedures and food handling practices to ensure ongoing compliance with regulatory requirements.
4.	Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety obligations and the safe operation of commercial kitchen equipment.
5.	Maintain accurate food safety documentation, cleaning schedules and operational records to support regulatory compliance.


Operational Administration
1.	Complete kitchen records relating to stock usage, food safety, cleaning schedules and wastage reporting accurately and on time.
2.	Assist management in identifying opportunities to improve kitchen efficiency, food quality, operational productivity and customer satisfaction.
3.	Support continuous improvement initiatives designed to enhance restaurant operations, service standards and overall business performance.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
1.	AQF Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Hospitality, Commercial Cookery or a closely related discipline.
2.	Minimum 2 years' full-time relevant experience as a Chef within a commercial restaurant environment.
3.	Demonstrated experience preparing and delivering high-quality à la carte cuisine within a busy commercial kitchen.
4.	Strong knowledge of HACCP principles, NSW Food Safety Standards and food handling legislation.
5.	Sound understanding of Workplace Health and Safety obligations within hospitality environments.
6.	Experience in menu planning, stock control, purchasing procedures and kitchen coordination.

KEY COMPETENCIES
1.	Strong culinary expertise across a broad range of commercial cooking techniques and food preparation methods.
2.	Demonstrated ability to coordinate kitchen operations during high-volume service periods while maintaining quality, consistency and efficiency.
3.	Sound understanding of menu development, food costing, recipe standardisation and portion control principles.
4.	Excellent organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
5.	Leadership capability to supervise, mentor and support kitchen staff within a collaborative team environment.
6.	Strong communication and interpersonal skills when working with management, kitchen staff and front-of-house pers

Employment: Permanent Full Time Contract 

Eligibility: Open to Everyone

Lead Facilities that Support Exceptional Healthcare

Are you an experienced maintenance professional ready to step into a leadership role? Join Yorke and Northern Local Health Network (YNLHN) as a Maintenance Supervisor, where you'll coordinate maintenance services across our healthcare facilities, ensuring safe, compliant and well-maintained environments for patients, staff and visitors.

This is an opportunity to combine your technical expertise with strong leadership skills while contributing to essential healthcare services that make a difference to local communities.

About the Role

As Maintenance Supervisor, you'll oversee the delivery of planned and reactive maintenance across a range of sites. You'll lead maintenance staff and contractors, coordinate projects, provide technical guidance, and ensure facilities remain safe, compliant and operating efficiently.

You'll also play an important role in managing fire and safety systems, supporting emergency preparedness, and maintaining high standards across buildings, equipment and infrastructure.

What You'll Bring

You'll be a practical and proactive leader with experience supervising maintenance teams in a complex facilities environment. Ideally, you'll have:

Relevant trade qualifications and extensive maintenance experience.

Experience supervising staff, contractors and maintenance projects.

Strong knowledge of building services, plant and equipment.

Excellent organisational and problem-solving skills.

A commitment to workplace safety, compliance and quality outcomes.

The ability to prioritise competing workloads across multiple sites.

Ready to Apply?

If you're ready to lead maintenance services that make a genuine difference, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today and help keep our healthcare facilities operating at their best.

About Us

YNLHN is committed to an inclusive and diverse workplace and encourages applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, culturally diverse backgrounds, LGBTIQA+SB communities, and people living with disability and-or neurodivergence. We support workplace adjustments and welcome you to share any access or support needs during recruitment and employment. 

A career in YNLHN offers diverse opportunities, strong career development, and the chance to live and work across a unique landscape including farming regions, coastline, vineyards, and the Southern Flinders Ranges. View the video below to learn more about working with us

Work with us - Yorke and Northern LHN

DHS National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) Worker Check
